PullRequest.Title: chat: fix Keep and Undo review synchronization
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Fix the editor/working-set integration gaps reported while testing #343685. Most are ordinary editing problems, not checkpoint problems.

- Open working-set files through the owning live review, honoring the existing diff preference, Alt reversal and side-by-side target. Existing comparisons follow later edits and close when their review resolves. Historical turn comparisons remain immutable; unavailable live reviews warn and fall back to recorded comparisons. Created/deleted-file fallbacks preserve preview focus and pinning.
- Wait for hunk decisions to reach the host publication and editor diff before navigating. Handle removed/final entries without reopening the resolved file, include newly published/replacement entries, and handle subscription errors without blocking the operation queue until its timeout.
- Choose pending entries consistently across overlays, commands, context keys and accessibility instead of letting a newer accepted Local entry hide Copilot review. Preserve the panel/global flag when the snapshot controller is created lazily, addressing another missing-until-reload path.
- Preserve selected/focused foreground/background color pairs instead of overriding their background on hover.
- Keep reversible checkpoint preview separate from host history: suppress only verified, fully restored working-set revisions, and restore visibility on Redo or a new host revision. Keep earlier edits and unrelated resources visible; report partial restoration failures and retain recovery through Undo/Redo.
- Preserve unsaved working copies instead of hiding their remaining edits: require save/revert before checkpoint writes, and retain review with a recoverable error if typing begins during restoration. Confirm absence after a failed delete validation rather than treating every stat failure as a missing file.

No authentication, Copilot SDK, protocol, telemetry or rollout-setting changes are included. The existing signed-in OSS profile was retained for the real-provider recordings.

## Issue coverage

| Issue | Change / validation |
| --- | --- |
| #343996 | Selected + hovered row keeps readable theme colors; recorded contrast improves from 1.225:1 to 6.115:1, exceeding 4.5:1. Real before/after recording and CSS validation. |
| #343994 | Verified the actual nested toolbar: Tab enters Keep, Right Arrow reaches Undo. Added an Enter-invocation regression; retained standard roving-tabindex behavior rather than adding inconsistent Tab stops. |
| #343992 | Real retained Local/Copilot reproduction and fixed recording; pending-owner regression plus lazy panel/inline initialization tests. The new lazy-panel regression failed against the original implementation. |
| #343888 | Real last-hunk reproduction and fixed next-file navigation; deferred success/failure, final-file and settling-state regressions. |
| #343883 | Real second agent edit updates the already visible diff; live-source and snapshot-fallback coverage. |
| #343868 | Real Start Over before/after, with checkpoint cursor, disk bytes and retained Redo asserted; lazy binding, initial loading, recomputation, errors, partial recovery and created/deleted-file regressions. |
| #343864 | Real file Undo restores disk and removes its live review diff; original snapshot diff remained open before the fix. |
| #343861 | Real row activation opens the diff; tests for preference, Alt, owning session and Session-only/unsupported-file fallbacks. |

Fixes #343996, fixes #343992, fixes #343888, fixes #343883, fixes #343868, fixes #343864, fixes #343861.
Addresses #343994 with verified standard keyboard behavior and regression coverage.

### Adversarial review

Completed independent correctness/scope reviews with GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-5.6 Sol, Gemini 4 Argon, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Opus 5 and Grok 4.7. Actionable findings were addressed, including lazy session binding, initial/error snapshot readiness, fallback coverage, partial restoration recovery, failed-Redo visibility and regression-test discovery. Existing partial-checkpoint projection limitations, ambiguous rename ownership and unrelated notebook behavior were explicitly kept out of scope instead of redesigning checkpointing.

### Copilot PR review

Addressed all seven findings across three Copilot review rounds:

- [Subscription errors](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/344133#discussion_r4370942806): readiness and post-decision waits observe both change and error events, read the current subscription state, and dispose their listeners.
- [Successive Undo after a failed restore](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/344133#discussion_r4370942852): only resources crossed by the current restore can gain or lose suppression. Previously verified, untouched revisions retain their state; a failed later checkpoint cannot become hidden when undoing an unrelated earlier one.
- [Created/deleted-file focus](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/344133#discussion_r4370942878): snapshot multi-diffs receive the row's preview, pinning and reveal options.
- [Replacement-revision visibility](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/344133#discussion_r4371011208): republish reused entries after their revision changes, so an observed entry list cannot stay empty when a newer host publication cancels a queued removal. The regression holds a real review update behind a deferred diff and observes the public entry list, rather than checking only the direct lookup.
- [Dirty working copies](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/344133#discussion_r4371271684): refuse checkpoint writes while an affected working copy has unsaved changes; recheck after writes so typing during restoration cannot make remaining edits disappear. Real text-file models verify preserved user/agent text, disk state, visible review and checkpoint recovery.
- [Delete stat failures](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/344133#discussion_r4371271706): verify absence through `resolve` after delete validation reports not-found, propagate real errors, and use the same strict existence check for rename recovery. Tests exercise the actual `FileService` validation path with both transient and persistent stat failures.
- [Deferred navigation arrivals](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/344133#discussion_r4371271725): retain the previous navigation position, match replacements by resource, and include newly published entries without reopening the starting resource.

Fourteen regression/control cases cover these paths; thirteen failed before their respective fixes, and all pass in the final suite run above. The initial CI failures also exposed three formatting issues and incomplete global-editing-session test stubs; those are corrected, with the full contribution suite now included.

### Live evidence

These are live Code OSS 1.144.0 recordings encoded with ffmpeg, using real signed-in Copilot/Local sessions and real file edits. They are not mock-provider or slideshow evidence. Captions sit above the captured screen. Each included step has a runtime/DOM/disk assertion; failed setup attempts and unvalidated trailing automation steps are excluded from the published clips.

### Limits

Windows/Linux live runs, full smoke/integration suites and every provider were not run. No claim is made to redesign partial checkpoint projections, infer ambiguous shared-file/rename provenance, or change the already released 1.143.1 build. Unsupported review files retain the recorded-diff fallback. This remains a draft for maintainer and Copilot review.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The exact remote boundary, nested serial loops, duplicate registrations, and URI construction are all directly traced. The number and size of files affect severity, not the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Remote `resourceRead` calls plus full snapshot bytes, Base64 decoding, and buffer allocations
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For N affected files and S registered views, this performs 2×N×S content reads. In the normal chat view S can be 2 because both `AgentHostEditReview` and `AgentHostSessionInputPills` register the same Working Set, producing up to four reads per file; the loops serialize files and sources.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Start Over and checkpoint Undo incur excessive remote I/O and serial network latency before any file restoration begins.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Checkpoint navigation resolved checkpoint edits and wrote crossed files; it had no pre-restore scan that fetched every visible Working Set snapshot or repeated that scan per UI source.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: `prepareRestore` now loops every registered source and file, issuing the added pair of full `readFile` calls before restoration. It neither deduplicates equivalent source revisions nor caches content URIs, even though `file.diff.originalURI` and `target.beforeContentUri` commonly wrap the same normalized before-content reference.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: New RIGHT lines 116-117 add two content reads inside nested source/file loops. The same diff also registers `_rawChanges` at `AgentHostEditReview.ts:352` and `checkpointSource` at `AgentHostSessionInputPills.ts:822` with the shared checkpoint review.
Findings.Title: Coalesce checkpoint snapshot comparisons
Findings.Impact: Undoing a checkpoint with a multi-file Working Set now fetches each baseline and before snapshot repeatedly. Agent-host content URIs resolve through `connection.resourceRead`, so remote sessions pay multiple round trips and transfer/decode the full file contents; duplicate UI sources repeat the same work.
Findings.Evidence: Both changeset diffs and checkpoint tool edits derive their before URI with `toAgentHostContentUri(normalized.beforeContentUri, ...)`; `AgentHostFileSystemProvider.readFile` services these URIs with `connection.resourceRead(..., Base64)` and decodes the returned bytes. `prepareRestore` awaits each file in sequence and does not coalesce duplicate sources or URIs.
Findings.Recommendation: Deduplicate files by channel/resource/revision across registered sources, short-circuit when the two content URIs are equal, and use an operation-scoped promise/content cache for remaining URI comparisons so each remote snapshot is fetched at most once.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed default call path, global sequencing, serial per-file work, and pre-diff direct-open behavior are explicit. Only the exact duration and typical working-set size vary by provider and file size.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Filesystem/content-reference reads, text-model loads, and editor-worker diff CPU for every pending working-set file
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The delay grows with the number and size of files in pending Working Set publications because `_update` awaits `_updateFile` serially for the full file list; each changed file reads snapshots and can run multiple diffs capped at 1 second each.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Opening a changed file can be delayed by seconds behind unrelated review reconciliation instead of opening immediately.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The working-set row used `openFile: true`, which called `editorService.openEditor` directly for the selected resource and did not wait for AgentHost review reconciliation.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new live-diff path calls `resolveEntry`, and this added line queues an empty task on the single session-wide `_updates` Sequencer, placing all previously queued `_update(files)` work on the row-open critical path.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added RIGHT line 361 explicitly awaits the global `_updates` Sequencer from `resolveEntry`; the newly added `_openFileDiff` awaits `session.resolveEntry` before opening the editor, whereas the deleted `openFile: true` path opened directly.
Findings.Title: Wait only for the selected file's review update
Findings.Impact: With the default `chat.editing.openChangedFileInDiffEditor=true`, clicking a working-set row while a multi-file host publication is being reconciled waits for every queued file before the editor opens. A turn touching many or large files therefore makes the row feel unresponsive even when the selected file is already available.
Findings.Evidence: `ChatSessionWorkingSet._openFileDiff` now awaits `AgentHostSnapshotController.resolveEntry`, which delegates here. `_updates` receives whole-publication `_update(files)` jobs at line 342; `_update` iterates files serially and `_updateFile` performs content reads, model resolution/reload, and editor-worker diff computation. The setting that takes this path defaults to true.
Findings.Recommendation: Track readiness per resource: return an already-current selected entry immediately, or await only the selected URI's reconciliation and fall back to the recorded diff on failure. Do not use the whole-session Sequencer as the row-open barrier.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The additional full-file read and remote provider call are explicit and occur on every write helper invocation. Savings are possible only when target bytes already equal the snapshot, which is atypical on normal checkpoint traversal; exact remote latency is environment-dependent.
Findings.PerformanceResource: One extra full-file read, transfer, buffer allocation, and byte comparison for every write-eligible checkpoint edit
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The extra I/O grows with total bytes and the number of edits across crossed checkpoints. Edits within one checkpoint launch concurrently, creating a read burst, while multiple checkpoints are processed serially.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Checkpoint Undo/Redo has higher latency and network/IPC traffic, especially for remote workspaces and large multi-file restores.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: For edit/create restoration, the controller read the checkpoint snapshot and immediately called `writeFile`; it did not read the current target file first.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: `_writeCheckpointFile` now reads the snapshot, then this added line reads and byte-compares the entire target, and only then performs the same write when content differs.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added RIGHT line 539 invokes `_readCheckpointFile(resource)` before every `_writeCheckpointFile` write; the deleted implementation in each edit branch directly read the snapshot and wrote it.
Findings.Title: Avoid pre-reading every normal checkpoint write
Findings.Impact: On an ordinary Undo/Redo the target content differs, so the new equality precheck does not save the write: it adds a full `resourceRead` before the existing `resourceWrite` for every edited file. Remote agent-host files therefore transfer the current file before writing the snapshot, increasing restore time and bandwidth.
Findings.Evidence: The helper is used for every Edit and content-bearing Create/Delete/Rename restoration. For `vscode-agent-host` targets, `IFileService.readFile` reaches `AgentHostFileSystemProvider.readFile`, which performs a remote `resourceRead` and Base64 decode. The PR's recovery tests show the equality check is needed only to make partially applied recovery idempotent, but it runs on all normal traversals.
Findings.Recommendation: Track which per-edit operations succeeded during a partial restore and apply equality/idempotency checks only when recovering those checkpoints; retain the previous direct snapshot-read/write path for normal checkpoint traversal.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a file from the chat working set in the default live diff
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Row activation calls `ChatSessionWorkingSet._openFileDiff`, awaits `session.resolveEntry`, waits for the Agent Host Working Set to settle, then queues behind the session-wide review `_updates` Sequencer before `editorService.openEditor` can run.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Wait for the Agent Host Changeset subscription to reach Ready/Error
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One subscription wait per live-diff open when the Working Set is unsettled; timeout is 30 seconds.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Working-set rows opened the selected file directly and did not wait on the Changeset subscription.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The editor cannot open until the provider publication settles.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read baseline/current snapshots and load or reload text models for pending review entries
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to two snapshot reads plus model work per changed file in each queued publication.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This review work existed, but row opening did not join its global queue, so unrelated files were off the open critical path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The added global Sequencer barrier makes all pending file reconciliation block the selected row's open.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Compute editor-worker string diffs for reconciled files
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Typically one or two computations per changed file, each configured with a 1-second computation cap.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Diff computation was asynchronous review maintenance rather than a prerequisite for opening the working-set row.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All queued computations now complete before the row open progresses.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Pending Working Set publications after a turn, with effective cardinality equal to all changed files awaiting reconciliation, not just the selected file; file sizes control snapshot transfer and diff CPU.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Working Set publications are globally serialized by one Sequencer, and `_update` awaits `_updateFile` in a serial file loop. Per-file baseline/current reads are paired, but different files do not reconcile concurrently.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: An already reconciled warm entry is cheap only when the global queue is empty. Cold/new/replacement entries load snapshots and models; there is no per-resource readiness path that lets a warm selected entry bypass unrelated queued files.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the default configuration, new await chain, single Sequencer, and serial per-file update loop are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical pending file counts and provider/model latency vary, but multi-file turns and immediate row activation are realistic; uncertainty affects severity rather than the global-barrier mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: the diff moves whole-session filesystem/model/diff work onto a single-file UI action's critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Start Over, Undo, or Redo an Agent Host checkpoint
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Resolve crossed checkpoint edits, call `checkpointReview.prepareRestore`, wait for registered Working Set sources, compare candidate snapshot contents, reject dirty working copies, then process checkpoints serially while each checkpoint launches its file operations concurrently.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the visible baseline and checkpoint before-content for comparison through Agent Host `resourceRead`
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two reads per affected non-created file per registered source; up to four reads/file when editor review and input pills expose the same Working Set.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Checkpoint navigation did not pre-scan visible Working Set snapshots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All comparisons complete before any checkpoint file restoration begins.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the current target before each checkpoint write and byte-compare it with the snapshot
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One extra full target read per write-eligible edit across crossed checkpoints; concurrent burst within each checkpoint.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The controller read the checkpoint snapshot and wrote it directly.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Normal changed-file restoration waits for an added remote read before the existing write.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write, delete, or move restored workspace resources
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One operation per checkpoint edit, with rename potentially followed by a content write.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same restore boundary existed, although failures previously stopped earlier and writes did not pre-read targets.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These operations remain the authoritative restore path and must finish before navigation completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read checkpoint snapshots used as write content
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One snapshot read per content-bearing restore edit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old implementation already read each snapshot before writing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required to supply bytes for each existing write.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N affected files, S registered Working Set sources (normally up to two for editor review plus input pills), C crossed checkpoints, and total file bytes. Projection comparison performs 2×N×S reads; normal writes add roughly one target pre-read per write-eligible edit.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Source readiness waits are parallel, but source/file comparison loops are serial. File operations within one checkpoint burst concurrently; crossed checkpoints remain serial under the undo/redo Sequencer.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No operation-scoped content cache or source/revision deduplication exists. Equal content URIs can be fetched twice, and the same Working Set can be compared again through both registered UI sources. Warm versus cold provider state does not eliminate explicit `resourceRead` calls.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: URI construction reaches the Agent Host filesystem provider's `resourceRead`, duplicate source registrations are explicit, and the nested loop/read cardinality is deterministic.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Local in-process hosts and small checkpoints reduce cost; remote hosts, large files, duplicate sources, and multi-file Start Over amplify it. The exact provider latency is unknown.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable twice: uncoalesced snapshot comparison fanout and unconditional target pre-reads add distinct remote I/O mechanisms to every restore.

Scenarios.Scenario: Keep or Undo a file or hunk and navigate to the next review entry
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The editor action awaits accept/reject; AgentHost invokes one Changeset operation, waits for the authoritative publication, waits for queued editor-review reconciliation, refreshes diff information for hunk decisions, then selects the next still-modified entry.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke the Agent Host Changeset accept/discard operation
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per Keep/Undo action, range-scoped for hunks or resource-scoped for files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The host operation already occurred, but editor actions did not await its completion before navigation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The decision cannot be authoritative until the host completes it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Wait for the post-decision Changeset publication or subscription error
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One wait per hunk decision when the subscription has not already advanced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Hunk operations could return before the authoritative publication and diff reconciliation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Navigation waits so it does not use stale review state.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Recompute the affected entry's editor diff after publication
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one explicit final diff readiness call per successful hunk decision, after normal review update processing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Navigation could proceed without this post-publication readiness wait.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Ensures next-change navigation observes the settled hunk list.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One host operation per user decision. Reconciliation can inspect the publication's Working Set files, while navigation scans the effective entry list once.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Decisions are serialized by `_operations`; Working Set updates are serialized by `_updates`. There is no concurrent host-operation burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Current subscription state is checked before installing a listener, and failures are observed rather than waiting for timeout. Existing entry/model state is reused; updated diff state is recomputed only after a hunk publication.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: operation, listener, sequencers, and navigation await chain are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Host publication latency varies, but the new wait is required for correct authoritative navigation and remains one operation per action.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: the added wait is an intentional ordering requirement, is bounded to one decision, and does not independently add a new fanout beyond the already reported global row-open barrier.

Scenarios.Scenario: Reactively render working-set, editor-overlay, and multi-diff review state
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Changeset/session observables project restored revisions, select pending entries across sessions, update working-set rows/context keys, and rebuild the multi-diff resource list in memory.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of active editing sessions, review files, entries, and restored revisions; effective cardinality is the current session working set rather than full chat history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous observable derivations run on state change; no limiter or asynchronous queue is involved.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Changeset file conversion is cached by observable identity in the pills, while checkpoint projection uses array scans without an index. Restored state is bounded by currently tracked restored revisions and is replaced/filter-updated on checkpoint navigation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the in-memory scaling shape; low for material user impact at realistic working-set sizes.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The new nested array scans can become quadratic for unusually large working sets, but no evidence establishes realistic rendering jank at expected cardinalities.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the work is in-memory and current evidence does not establish a concrete performance regression threshold.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 24 changed files and paginated large diffs. Submitted three findings: whole-session reconciliation on a single-row open path, uncoalesced remote snapshot comparisons during checkpoint restore, and unconditional target pre-reads before normal checkpoint writes. No qualifying regression-fix learning record was established.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
